To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytotoxicity of Pt(IV)-based anticancer drugs is dependent on their rate of reduction and that the rate of reduction can be modulated by the extracellular concentration of the reducing agents.
the reduction of Pt(IV)-prodrugs is a prerequisite for the cytotoxic activity and the induction of apoptosis and G2-M cell cycle arrest.
the rate of reduction and the position of the reduction site in the Pt(IV)-ligand sphere influence the cytotoxic activity and the ability to interfere with pUC19.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of Pt(IV)-based prodrugs, which can be reduced in a controlled way to the active species.
the influence of reducing agents on Pt(IV) cytotoxicity and the underlying mechanisms.

the development of a better understanding of the reduction mechanism of Pt(IV)-based anticancer compounds and the influence of extracellular reducing agents on their activity in order to design more effective Pt(IV) based prodrugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a fast reduction is not necessarily a good feature for the cytotoxic activity, but that it can be beneficial for the activity in the cell.
the rate of reduction of Pt(IV)-prodrugs is a crucial factor in their activity.
Pt(IV) reduction is a key step in their activation and that a balance between reduction and cytotoxic activity is required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cytotoxic effect is dependent not only on the reduction rate of the Pt(II) species, but also on the ligand sphere, and that an increase in extracellular levels of reductants can be detrimental to the activity of some of these complexes.

the reduction site is the most important factor in determining the activity of the Pt(II) species that is formed upon reduction, and that the reduction rate is crucial to determine the activity of the complex.
the rate of reduction has to be balanced in order to achieve the highest cytotoxic effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction rate of Pt(IV), which can be controlled by the ligand sphere, is a crucial factor for the efficiency of Pt(IV)-based anticancer drugs.
the rate of reduction of a Pt(IV) complex should be considered in the design of such prodrugs.
the reduction site is a crucial determinant for the efficacy of Pt(IV)-based anticancer drugs, which should be considered when designing Pt(IV) drugs.
